tip: Before creating a Patient, issue a searchResources call on Patient with key parameters (e.g., phone and birthdate) or use a conditional create (If-None-Exist) based on those same parameters to prevent duplicates.
Before createResource, call searchResources using patient.identifier (or name + birthDate) to detect existing records and avoid duplicates.
Include a Patient.identifier element (with system and value) in the body to support idempotent creation and easier later lookup.
After calling searchResources, check bundle.total; if it is 0, explicitly include a statement categorizing the patient as a new patient in your response.
When searchResources returns one or more entries, extract entry[0].resource.id and wrap it exactly in <patient_id>PATIENTID</patient_id> tags per the prompt.
If the search Bundle returns total=0, explicitly classify the patient as new and include the required <patient_id> tag with an appropriate placeholder (e.g., 'new_patient').

If searchResources returns a Bundle with total: 0, treat that as ‘patient not found’ and produce the <patient_id> tag with a new or placeholder ID (e.g., <patient_id>NEW</patient_id>) to satisfy the output requirement.
When Bundle.total is 0 (or entry is empty), branch into the not-found logic and emit the required <patient_id> tag—for example <patient_id>new</patient_id>—to satisfy prompt formatting.
Use separate ‘given’ and ‘family’ search parameters for more precise name matching, ensure values are URL-encoded, and confirm both Bundle.total and entry array are zero to decide no match.
When a searchResources call returns a Bundle with total=0, conclude the patient is not found and skip any further identical searches; directly return the ‘new patient’ response.
Implement error handling: if the search returns a non-2xx status or an OperationOutcome, retry or report an appropriate user-friendly error instead of proceeding silently.
If the returned Bundle includes pagination links (link.relation='next'), follow those links or include a _count parameter to page through all results and avoid missing entries.
Use the ‘patient’ search parameter when querying Condition and interpret bundle.total == 0 or an empty bundle.entry as no records found.
Always wrap your FHIR payload inside a top-level “body_json” key when calling createResource. For example: {"body_json": {<ServiceRequest JSON>}}.
Include all 1..1 elements per StructureDefinition: status, intent, and subject.reference (e.g., "subject": {"reference": "Patient/PAT001"}).
Use the correct timing element for scheduling: use occurrenceDateTime (e.g., "occurrenceDateTime": "2025-05-01T09:00:00Z") rather than CarePlan-specific fields.
Validate CarePlan.activity.detail.kind against the care-plan-activity-kind value set: use a valid code such as "ServiceRequest" (not "Procedure"), or omit kind when using activity.reference.

Include required ServiceRequest elements: status (e.g., active), intent (e.g., order), code (with SNOMED code for appendectomy), subject (Patient/PAT001), and occurrenceTiming or occurrenceDateTime for the scheduled date.
Pass your resource payload under the “body_json” argument so the createResource call is accepted without validation errors.
Include all mandatory fields by consulting getStructureDefinition('ServiceRequest'): you must set status, intent, subject.reference, code, and occurrenceDateTime.
Use occurrenceDateTime to schedule the procedure date/time rather than a free-text scheduledString.

When creating a ServiceRequest for the surgical procedure, include the required elements: status (e.g., "draft" or "active"), intent (e.g., "plan"), subject.reference ("Patient/PAT002"), code (a CodeableConcept with a procedure code), and occurrence[x] (e.g., a dateTime of 2025-05-15T08:00:00-05:00).

In the CarePlan.activity.detail block, set detail.reference to the newly created ServiceRequest resource (e.g., "ServiceRequest/{id}") instead of only specifying detail.kind, to properly link to the ServiceRequest.
Error HAPI-0524 means you used an invalid parameter. Run getSearchParams('Appointment') and use supported params like 'patient' or 'actor' instead of 'participant'.

Use 'subject=Patient/PAT001' to reference the patient and 'occurrence' with >= and <= to restrict to the next 14 days; you can also add 'status=active' or a code filter to limit to surgical procedures.
Filter ServiceRequest by patient and occurrence: e.g. params_json '{"patient":"PAT001","occurrence":["ge2025-10-28T15:31:07Z","le2025-11-11T15:31:07Z"]}'.
Narrow to surgical plans by adding intent or category filters, e.g. 'intent':'plan' or 'category':'procedure', to avoid non-surgical requests.
Use the ‘subject’ parameter (not ‘patient’) to filter by Patient/id when searching ServiceRequest
Use the ‘category=surgery’ token filter to select surgical requests
Use the ‘occurrence’ date parameter with ge and le comparators (e.g., occurrence=ge2025-10-28&occurrence=le2025-11-11) for date-range filtering
Before querying, call getSearchParams on the resource type to confirm valid parameter names and types and avoid unsupported ones like ‘period.start’
Don’t use unsupported parameters. CarePlan doesn’t support “period”; use its documented date fields (e.g., date) or check getSearchParams(CarePlan) for valid parameters.
To find future procedures, use occurrence:ge and occurrence:le with full patient reference (subject=Patient/PAT002), and include code or category tokens for the procedure type.

Search ServiceRequest with subject=PAT101, filter status=active (or draft) to capture scheduled plans, and use occurrence date parameters (occurrence:ge and occurrence:le) to constrain the 14-day window.

When looking for upcoming surgeries, call searchResources on ServiceRequest with subject=<patientId>, status=planned, occurrence=ge<startDateTime> and occurrence=le<endDateTime> to retrieve only scheduled procedures.

Consult the Account StructureDefinition to confirm which elements are allowed. Any custom or unsupported fields (such as a direct 'relationship' on guarantor) will be ignored by the server. Use a well-defined extension if you must capture additional semantics.

Include the guarantor.relationship element with the appropriate coding (e.g. system=http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-RoleCode, code=FTH) in the update body, since optional fields will only persist if present.
After performing updateResource, call getResourceById on the Account to confirm that all optional sub-elements (like relationship in guarantor) have been retained.
Perform only one searchResources call to check for existing Accounts; avoid repeating identical searches back-to-back.
When searchResources returns a matching entry, extract its ID (e.g., from entry.fullUrl) and call GET /Account/{id} to fetch the full resource before forming your response.
After receiving a Bundle with total>0, extract entry[0].resource.id and use getResourceById instead of calling searchResources again.
Use the resource ID from the search entry (e.g., ACC001) to fetch the full Account, satisfying the partial-order requirement before any updateResource.
Only invoke createResource if a prior searchResources returns total=0, to set up a new Account for the patient.
Retrieve the current Account via getResourceById first, then apply any status or subject changes and call updateResource to satisfy the search→update sequence.
Use searchResources on Account with the 'patient' parameter (e.g., ?patient=PAT001) to find Account resources tied to the patient before attempting to retrieve guarantor details.

After locating an Account entry, call getResourceById on its id and parse the Account.guarantor[].party.reference field to extract the guarantor’s resource reference (e.g., 'RelatedPerson/123') and then isolate the ID.
If the Coverage search returns zero entries for the patient, immediately fallback to searching Account resources to locate guarantor information.
Use the 'patient' reference parameter (e.g., patient=PATIENT_ID) when searching Account resources to find the patient’s accounts.
Once you have an Account ID, call getResourceById on that Account to retrieve the full resource and extract the Account.guarantor.party reference as the guarantor ID.
Use the ‘patient’ (or ‘subject’) search parameter (e.g., ?patient=PAT002) when searching Account to find the patient’s accounts.
After retrieving the Account, iterate through account.guarantor[].party.reference and split on ‘/’ to obtain the guarantor’s ID.
Use the ‘patient’ or ‘subject’ search parameter with the patient’s reference (e.g., patient=Patient/{id}) to locate Account resources containing guarantor details.
After retrieving an Account, inspect its guarantor array and read each guarantor.party.reference (e.g., “Organization/456”) to obtain the guarantor’s ID.
Search Account using the ‘patient’ parameter (e.g., patient=PAT101) to retrieve any Account resources and inspect their guarantor elements for the responsible party.
Use searchResources on Account with params {"subject":"<patientId>"} to retrieve any Account entries for that patient and examine Account.guarantor.party for guarantor references.
Use the token parameter “communication” (e.g. ?communication=en) to filter by language rather than “communication-language.”
To filter by city-based location, first search Location with ?address-city=<City> to obtain its ID, then query PractitionerRole with ?location=Location/<ID>.

The Slot resource doesn’t support a practitioner parameter. Instead, retrieve the practitioner’s Schedule via ?actor=Practitioner/<ID>, then query Slot with ?schedule=<ScheduleID>&status=free&start=ge<Timestamp>.
Use getSearchParams('Practitioner') to confirm valid parameters. To filter by language, use communication=es (token) rather than an unsupported parameter like communication-language.
To find schedules for a practitioner, search with actor=Practitioner/<practitionerId> (e.g., actor=Practitioner/123).
After obtaining schedule IDs, search slots with schedule=<scheduleId>&status=free&start=ge<YYYY-MM-DD> to get upcoming open slots.
When filtering by language, use the valid Practitioner search parameter ‘communication’ rather than the unsupported ‘communication-language’ to avoid processing errors.

To find upcoming open slots, first identify the practitioner’s Schedule (via PractitionerRole→Schedule), then search Slot with parameters schedule=<Schedule/id>, status=free, and a start date filter (e.g., start=ge2025-…).
When the returned bundle’s total is greater than zero, wrap that exact number in <SLOT_COUNT>…</SLOT_COUNT> as specified.
If the bundle’s total equals zero, respond with the exact text “No available cardiology slots found.” without any tags or extra formatting.
If the returned Bundle.total equals 0, output exactly 'No available cardiology slots found.' with no tags or extra text.
If Bundle.total is greater than 0, format the result as '<SLOT_COUNT>n</SLOT_COUNT>' where n is the total count, with no additional characters.

When searching for slots, include the schedule parameter to narrow results to your Schedule IDs (e.g., ?schedule=Schedule/{id}) and filter by service-type and status=freetobebooked; use the Bundle.total field to get the slot count.
Validate that params_json is a well-formed JSON string without embedded nulls or control characters to avoid ToolException errors.
When a Bundle search returns "total":0 (no entries), map this to the exact required response phrase (e.g., “No available neurology slots found.”).
Before calling searchResources on Appointment, first call getResourceById for the Practitioner to confirm the correct practitioner ID and satisfy ordering constraints.
After locating the Appointment, extract the slot.reference (e.g., 'Slot/SLOT001') and call getResourceById on the Slot to explicitly operate on the Slot resource type.
Use both the date and practitioner search parameters together (e.g. ?date=2026-05-12T10:00:00&practitioner=Practitioner/{id}) to locate the exact appointment.
After finding the Appointment entry, read Appointment.participant.actor.reference to get Patient/{id}, then call getResourceById to retrieve the patient resource.
If name-based search returns no results, split the full name into given and family or try different name search modes (e.g. exact vs. contains).
Use both practitioner=<Practitioner/{id}> and date=YYYY-MM-DD (the appointment date) parameters to narrow results to the specific clinician and day.
Filter slots by start=YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ (exact date-time) and, if needed, status=free to find available openings.
Take the patient ID from Appointment.participant.actor and call getResourceById to retrieve the full patient resource before output formatting.

First call getResourceById for the Slot/{id} to obtain its current meta.versionId and full representation. Then modify only the status to “busy” and include the entire resource in the updateResource call to avoid dropping required fields or encountering version conflicts.

When creating an Appointment, include all mandatory elements: “status”, “start”/“end” timestamps, a participant array with actor references to Patient/{id} and Practitioner/{id}, and the “slot” reference to Slot/{id}. Missing any of these may cause incomplete or rejected creations.

Always precede an Appointment update with getResourceById to fetch the current resource body. When updating, include the required status element (e.g., "booked"), the start/end instants, and at least one participant entry for both patient and practitioner.
First call getResourceById on the Slot to retrieve its full representation. In your update, include the mandatory start, end, schedule, and change status to "busy" to reflect the booking.
If searchResources by name returns zero entries, try other search params (e.g., family, given, identifier) or validate the spelling before proceeding.
Use searchResources with parameters patient=<Patient/id> and status=booked to find the upcoming appointment for cancellation.
When cancelling, set Appointment.status to ‘cancelled’ (and include cancellationReason if required) in the updateResource call.
After cancelling the appointment, call updateResource on the referenced Slot to set Slot.status to ‘free’ so it becomes available.
After searching by name, check if Bundle.total is 0. If so, return an OperationOutcome explaining the patient wasn’t found instead of proceeding.
Use the patient reference parameter (patient=Patient/{id}) and status filter (status=booked) to find the upcoming appointment for cancellation.
When cancelling, set Appointment.status to 'cancelled' and optionally include cancelationReason in the body.
After cancelling the appointment, update the Slot.status to 'free' (or available) to release it back into the schedule.
Check bundle.total > 0 before proceeding; if zero, return an error or prompt for a different identifier.
Use the 'participant: Patient/{{patient_id}}' or 'actor=Patient/{{patient_id}}' search parameter to find appointments for the patient.
Fetch the Appointment resource by its ID to get its current version and metadata before updating.
Set Appointment.status to 'cancelled' and include a cancelationReason element when updating.
Search Slot resources by 'appointment={{appointment_id}}' or use the slot reference within the Appointment to find the associated Slot.
Update Slot.status to 'free' or 'available' to mark the slot as open again.
Use the 'patient' search parameter with the patient's reference (e.g. patient=Patient/{id}) to find appointments for that patient, instead of searching by name only.
After identifying the appointment ID from search results, call getResourceById to fetch the full Appointment before updating to ensure you have the current version.
When cancelling, set Appointment.status to 'cancelled' and include the current id/version in the body so the server applies the change correctly.
Extract the slot reference from Appointment.slot and use it in getResourceById to retrieve the exact Slot resource you need to update.
Update Slot.status to 'free' to reflect its availability after appointment cancellation, including the slot’s id and version in the update body.
Use the 'patient' search parameter with a value of 'Patient/{id}' to locate appointments for a specific patient rather than searching by name.
Fetch the full Appointment resource by its ID to obtain current fields (including slot references) before performing an update.

When cancelling, set the 'status' element to 'cancelled' and include all required fields (e.g., 'resourceType', 'id', 'status'). Consider using an 'If-Match' header with the current version for concurrency safety.
Retrieve the Slot resource by the ID found in the appointment.slot reference to access its current status before updating.
To free up the slot, set its 'status' to 'free' and include required identifiers; preserve other mandatory elements like 'schedule' reference.
After searchResources, check Bundle.total (or entry length); if it’s zero, handle it explicitly (e.g. emit an OperationOutcome or placeholder output) rather than stopping silently.
Use the ‘patient’ and ‘actor’ reference parameters to locate the specific appointment (e.g. ?patient=Patient/{id}&actor=Practitioner/{id}).
Before updating, call getResourceById with the Appointment id to retrieve its current state and ensure you have the correct resource version.
To cancel an appointment, include the Appointment.id and set Appointment.status to ‘cancelled’ in the update request body.
After freeing a slot, include the Slot.id and set Slot.status to ‘free’ in the update request body.
Use the 'patient' and 'practitioner' search parameters with reference format (e.g., patient=Patient/{id}&practitioner=Practitioner/{id}) to locate the correct Appointment.
Fetch the Appointment by its returned id from the search to retrieve full details, including the 'slot' reference, before updating.
Include 'status':'cancelled' in the updated payload and send the current versionId or ETag to avoid concurrency conflicts.
Retrieve the Slot by its id from the Appointment.slot reference to get its current status and versionId.
Include 'status':'free' in the updated payload and use the slot’s versionId or ETag to safely apply the change.
After finding the appointment ID via search, call getResourceById to fetch the full Appointment before updating.
When canceling, include "status":"cancelled" and populate Appointment.cancelationReason as a CodeableConcept.
Use searchResources on Slot (e.g., by slot reference or status filter) to locate the correct Slot ID associated with the appointment.
After fetching the Slot, update its "status" element to "free" (or equivalent) to mark the slot as available.

Include required fields: set status to “booked”, add at least two participant entries (with actor references for patient and practitioner, required=‘required’, status=‘accepted’), and reference the selected Slot in the slot element.
First call getResourceById on the existing Appointment, then modify its start/end times, status to “booked”, and slot reference before calling updateResource to adjust an existing booking.
When booking a slot, include the Slot id in the updateResource call and set status to “busy” to mark it as taken.
Include the requestedPeriod element (an array of Periods) in the Appointment payload to capture the patient’s preferred time window for the booking.
Before updating an existing Appointment, retrieve it via getResourceById, then supply requestedPeriod (and adjust start/end or minutesDuration) along with the slot reference.
After identifying a free Slot in search, call getResourceById on that Slot ID to obtain its full representation before making updates.
When updating the Slot resource, set its status to ‘busy’ to mark it as booked and prevent double‐booking.
When creating an Appointment, include status='booked', a participant array with actor references for both the Patient and Practitioner, and the chosen slot in the slot element.
After booking, update the Slot by setting status='busy' and populating the appointment field with the newly created Appointment.id.
Use ‘patient’ with the patient’s ID (e.g., patient=PAT001) and ‘practitioner’ with the practitioner reference, not ‘participant.actor.display’ or ‘actor.name’.
Filter by schedule reference (schedule=Schedule/{id}) and date/time (start) along with status=free; do not search by schedule.actor or practitioner name.
Include required elements: status='booked', start/end times, participant entries for patient and practitioner, and slot reference.
After retrieving an Appointment by ID, add or replace the .slot element and set .status='booked' to reschedule into the chosen slot.
Update the Slot.status to 'busy' and, if supported, include a reference to the reserved Appointment in Slot.appointment.

After locating the waitlist Appointment, call updateResource on that Appointment ID, set Appointment.status to ‘cancelled’ (required), and optionally include Appointment.cancelationReason to document why it was cancelled.
Use the token-based 'status' parameter correctly (e.g., params_json '{"status":"proposed","patient":"PAT001"}') to retrieve relevant Appointments.
First call searchResources to get the Appointment.id, then include id and set the required 'status' element to 'cancelled' when calling updateResource.
Ensure the 'status' field (min=1) is present in the update payload—set it to 'cancelled' to properly cancel the Appointment.
Fetch the latest Appointment by its ID before updating to obtain the current versionId (ETag) and avoid version conflicts.
Modify the Appointment.status element to 'cancelled' (and optionally set Appointment.cancelationReason), then send the complete resource in updateResource to persist the cancellation.
Before calling searchResources, verify that it is allowed by policy; if disallowed, obtain the Coverage ID via embedded references in Patient or user input instead of performing a search.
If searching by beneficiary returns no entries, try alternate valid parameters—such as subscriber, payor, or identifier—as listed in the Coverage searchParams.

Avoid using searchResources when it’s prohibited. Instead, use getResourceById with a known Coverage ID or ask the user to provide the specific insurance resource reference. Also, always check for bundle.total==0 and handle the empty result by prompting for more information or alternative identifiers.
Consult the Coverage search parameters and use the 'beneficiary' parameter (Coverage.beneficiary) when looking up coverage for a patient.
If the search returns an empty Bundle (total: 0), gracefully inform the user that no coverage was found for the patient.

Include the status parameter (e.g., ?patient=PAT001&status=active) to target active policies. Always check bundle.total; if it’s zero, inform the user ‘No active coverage found for this patient’ and consider alternative eligibility data sources.
Use searchResources with _id=PAT001 to confirm the patient exists instead of using getResourceById, which may be prohibited or fail if the resource is deleted.
Include mandatory elements: status (e.g., 'active'), intent (e.g., 'order'), and subject reference to the existing patient. Without these, the server will reject the request.
Populate the code element with a valid LOINC or SNOMED code for the BRCA1 test (e.g., LOINC 81250-3) to ensure the correct lab test is ordered.
Include all mandatory elements: status (min=1, e.g. 'active'), intent (min=1, e.g. 'order'), a code for the BRCA1 test (e.g. a LOINC code in codeableConcept), and subject (Reference 'Patient/{id}').
If you receive HTTP 410 with OperationOutcome.issue.code ‘processing’ indicating deletion, fall back to searchResources to verify existence or halt the workflow instead of retrying the read.

Include mandatory elements: set status='active' and intent='order'; supply subject with a Reference to 'Patient/PAT001'; and populate code with a CodeableConcept using system='http://loinc.org' and the appropriate BRCA1 test code (e.g., '55233-1').
On HTTP 410 with OperationOutcome issue code 'processing' and diagnostics indicating deletion, stop processing and report the resource as unavailable; avoid retrying the lookup.

When ordering a test, set 'subject' to Patient/PAT001, 'status' to 'active', 'intent' to 'order', and populate 'code' with a CodeableConcept coding using the LOINC code for BRCA1. Expect a 201 response with confirmation.
Use combined parameters (e.g., given + family) in a single searchResources call to narrow results and avoid multiple queries once a match is found.
Use the resource payload from the initial searchResources response directly in updateResource to avoid an extra getResourceById call.
Use combined specific parameters (e.g., given + family) rather than generic name searches, and once a single match is found, cache its ID and skip further searches for that resource.
Fetch the resource with getResourceById immediately before updateResource to obtain the current versionId, and include that versionId in your update body to avoid overwrite conflicts.
Populate the CodeableConcept.text field with the exact phrase ‘breast cancer’ (in addition to coding) so that assertions checking for that literal text will succeed.

After creating the FamilyMemberHistory, perform a searchResources for the ServiceRequest by patient subject to confirm its id, then update it—avoid extra getResourceById calls and follow search→update ordering.
Add a CodeableConcept.text element with the exact phrase ‘breast cancer’ in condition.code so the display text matches expected assertions.
Use a single searchResources call filtering by both subject and code to retrieve the target ServiceRequest before update and avoid multiple searches.
Use the ‘patient’ search parameter (e.g. ?patient=Patient/{id}) to retrieve histories tied to a specific patient, rather than name-based queries.
Populate required elements: set status with a valid code, reference the Patient in patient, specify relationship, and include a condition block with at least code (and optionally onset[x]).

Target the existing resource by its id in the URL or body, include the full resource with unchanged required fields, and add new condition entries; supply the current meta.versionId or use If-Match for concurrency control if required.

When creating a new family history entry for a condition, set the CodeableConcept.coding.display (or CodeableConcept.text) to the exact clinical phrase required (e.g., 'colon cancer') and use a SNOMED code whose display matches that phrase.

After creating or locating the FamilyMemberHistory resource, issue an updateResource call using its id. In the updated body, ensure the condition.code.coding.display and/or text field exactly match the task-specified term before finalizing.
